Description:
  TerseSharp - token-efficient Roslyn MCP server for C# and .NET.

Usage:
  terse [command] [options]

Options:
  -?, -h, --help  Show help and usage information
  --version       Show version information

Commands:
  serve        Run the MCP server over stdio.
  guard        Hook entry point: reads a Claude Code PreToolUse payload on stdin and denies built-in tools on C#/.NET source.
  install      Register TerseSharp with your MCP clients.
  uninstall    Remove TerseSharp from your MCP clients.
  doctor       Verify SDK, MSBuild, client registration and workspace load.
  call <tool>  Call one MCP tool of this binary from the shell and print its response, so a claim about a freshly built terse can be tested without hand-writing JSON-RPC.

result.stdout:
Description:
  Run the MCP server over stdio.

Usage:
  terse serve [options]

Options:
  --workspace <workspace>            Solution or project to load at startup.
  --read-only                        Expose read tools only.
  --no-watch                         Do not watch the workspace for external file changes. TERSE_WATCH=0 does the same.
  --max-workspaces <max-workspaces>  How many solutions stay loaded at once; the least recently used is unloaded beyond that. Default 4. TERSE_MAX_WORKSPACES does the same. A large solution costs gigabytes, so set 1 when you only ever work in one.
  --idle-minutes <idle-minutes>      Drop a workspace's Roslyn compilations after it has been idle this long, and return the memory. Default 15; 0 keeps them for the life of the process. TERSE_IDLE_MINUTES does the same. The next semantic call re-realizes what it needs.
  --tools <tools>                    Which tools to advertise: core, a ~20-tool subset, or all, the whole surface. Unset, it advertises the families the loaded solution holds - the default - and an unrecognised value falls back to that. Every other tool still answers when called by name; only the advertised list shrinks, which is the measured lever on tool-selection accuracy. TERSE_TOOLS does the same.
  -?, -h, --help                     Show help and usage information

Description:
  Hook entry point: reads a Claude Code PreToolUse payload on stdin and denies built-in tools on C#/.NET source.

Usage:
  terse guard [options]

Options:
  --post-batch    Read a Claude Code PostToolBatch payload instead, and nudge the next response to batch its independent calls when the batch was one read-only terse call - except the half held out by a hash of its tool_use id, which is only logged to ~/.terse/batch-nudge.log.
  -?, -h, --help  Show help and usage information

result.stdout:
Description:
  Register TerseSharp with your MCP clients.

Usage:
  terse install [options]

Options:
  --client <client>        claude-code, cursor, vscode or windsurf. Omit to detect.
  --workspace <workspace>  Solution or project to load at startup.
  --skill                  Also install the agent skill that teaches which TerseSharp tool replaces which built-in.
  --guard                  Also install a Claude Code PreToolUse hook that blocks Read/Grep/Edit on C#/.NET and XAML files, and a PostToolBatch hook that asks for independent calls in one response after a lone read-only terse call.
  -?, -h, --help           Show help and usage information

Description:
  Call one MCP tool of this binary from the shell and print its response, so a claim about a freshly built terse can be tested without hand-writing JSON-RPC.

Usage:
  terse call <tool> [options]

Arguments:
  <tool>  MCP tool name, e.g. get_file_outline.

Options:
  --workspace <workspace>  Solution or project to load at startup.
  --json <json>            Tool arguments as a JSON object, e.g. '{"path": "src/App.cs"}'. Omit for none.
  -?, -h, --help           Show help and usage information
